# IDS Model Check

> Free, MIT-licensed checker for buildingSMART IDS 1.0 (Information Delivery Specification) files against IFC building models (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3; STEP .ifc, ifcXML or .ifczip). Runs in the browser with nothing uploaded, or as a dependency-free Node command line. Exports BCF 2.1 issues, CSV and JSON.

- Page: https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/
- Source: https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/ids-model-check
- Accuracy: 334 of 334 of buildingSMART's IDS test pairs (suite commit 870f9c4, 2026-09-25); same verdicts and failing elements as IfcTester on five real models, except multiple xs:pattern restrictions, where it follows XSD and the suite (patterns are alternatives).

## Use

- Browser: drop a model (.ifc, .ifcxml or .ifczip) and a .ids, read each specification's result and the failing elements, download BCF/CSV/JSON.
- CLI: `node cli.mjs model.ifc|.ifcxml|.ifczip spec.ids [--json] [--bcf out.bcfzip]`; exit 0 all pass, 1 a specification fails or is invalid, 2 error.
- IDS audit with no model: `node cli.mjs --audit spec.ids` (or "Audit the IDS only" on the page) reports specifications that are invalid against the IFC schema: unknown or lower-case classes, attributes a class lacks or has only as derived/inverse, values compared with lists/objects/selects, malformed numbers, integers and booleans, patterns on numbers, unknown dataTypes, prohibited specifications with requirements; standard property and quantity sets against buildingSMART's templates for IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3 ADD2 (Pset_/Qto_ names and properties the standard lacks, with the nearest standard name; a dataType the template does not give; a set the selected classes cannot carry), as buildingSMART's IDS-Audit-tool does. Flags 26 of buildingSMART's 27 invalid IDS test files and none of the 307 valid ones, and all 5 property set files in the IDS-Audit-tool's invalid set. A model check still runs a specification whose only fault is a property set template one, with a warning.
- IDS editor (https://marisstella.app/ids-model-check/editor.html): build an IDS 1.0 file by picking an IFC class, a standard Pset_/Qto_ set that class can carry (its own, an ancestor's, or for a type object its occurrence's) and a property; writes the template's dataType, offers the standard enumeration values, lists subclasses (IDS matches exact classes), audits live, downloads the .ids or sends it to the checker. Every offered class/set/property (203,433 specifications over IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3) audits with no error or warning; a 15,102-specification sample validates against ids.xsd in IfcTester. Opens an existing IDS (importIds): editable rows where the page can hold a facet unchanged, the rest kept as written; 64 of 64 public IDS files, 12 of 12 IDS-Audit-tool valid files and 187 of 187 buildingSMART pass cases write back asking the same, none made invalid against ids.xsd (eval/editor-open-2026-11-16.md). Open a model to write for (inventory.mjs modelInventory, run in worker.mjs): lists the model's classes with counts and the sets their objects carry, offers the carried standard sets first and the model's own sets (any name outside the case-sensitive Pset_/Qto_ prefixes, e.g. Revit's PSet_Revit_Dimensions) as editable rows with the data type the model writes; on 4 real exports 347 of 395 (class, set) pairs were own sets and 21 of 122 standard properties used a data type the template does not give (eval/model-inventory-2026-11-16.md). Several classes per specification (2026-11-17): an "Also applies to" list written as one entity facet; the page offers only the sets, attributes and predefined types every class shares (commonSets, commonAttributes, commonPredefinedTypes); 29 class-list specifications in 11 public IDS files now open as editable, 81.1% of public facets editable (was 79.4%), all still writing back the same (eval/several-classes-2026-11-17.md). A model's values (2026-11-17): each property row lists the values the open model holds (inventory.mjs reads them with the checker's PropertyFacet.values, SI units) and offers "Allow exactly these values" (one-of) or "Use the model's range"; range bounds are rounded outward (outwardBound) because IDS ranges take no tolerance, and on 4 real exports 364 of 752 ranges from values as displayed failed their own model while all 1,014 requirements built from the offers pass; "one of" works on any text property or attribute, 82.0% of public facets editable (eval/model-values-2026-11-17.md). Attribute values and classification codes (2026-11-17): attribute rows (Name, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType) and classification rows offer the model's values and each system's codes (modelAttributes, modelCodes); on 4 real exports all 242 attribute one-of offers with no empty value pass their model; objects classified in a system with an empty code (143 of 210 Uniformat-classified elements and 93 of 134 type objects in the Schultz Residence Revit export) are counted, and "Require a code" writes a .+ pattern that fails exactly them (eval/model-attr-codes-2026-11-17.md). Conditions beyond the class (2026-11-17): "Narrow it" adds property, attribute, classification, material or place rows to a specification's applicability (written with no cardinality); with a model open each says how many of the class's objects it keeps (appMatchCount, equal to the checker's applicable count on 11 tested conditions, null where the inventory cannot tell); opened files' applicability facets open as rows when they write back unchanged: 83.5% of public facets editable (was 82.0%), IDS-Audit-tool valid files 21.5% (was 9.7%) (eval/applicability-rows-2026-11-17.md). Numeric attribute ranges (2026-11-17): real and integer attributes (OverallHeight, Elevation, NumberOfRiser) get a "between" mode and "Use the model's range", written with an xs:double or xs:integer base; boolean attributes are asked true/false (attributeValueKind); on 4 real exports and the sample house 27 of 27 numeric and 6 of 6 boolean requirements built from the model pass it, same verdict as IfcTester on all 33; attributes are compared in the model's own units, not SI, in this checker and in IfcTester (eval/model-attr-ranges-2026-11-17.md). Values with no dataType (2026-11-17): an opened property value with no dataType becomes an editable row that writes none (typeRow adds the template's type on request); 84.9% of public facets editable (was 83.6%); a standard boolean written TRUE with no dataType matched 0 sample walls in this checker and 2 in IfcTester 0.8.0, so the row and the audit warn (eval/untyped-values-2026-11-17.md). Accept any data type (2026-11-17, untypeRow): a standard-set row whose open model writes the property in another type (Reference as IFCLABEL, not IFCIDENTIFIER) can drop its dataType; on 2 real exports 791 of 966 objects failed only for their type, none do with no dataType, audit clean, same verdict as IfcTester 0.8.0 on 21 of 21; real-number values stay presence-only because checkers read them apart (eval/model-any-type-2026-11-17.md). Logic in editor.mjs (setsFor, appMatchCount, typeRow, untypeRow, propertiesOf, modelSets, modelValueOffer, outwardBound, specClassNames, buildIds, importIds).
- CI: `action.yml` (GitHub composite action: `uses: Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo/ventures/ids-model-check@main` with `models` and `ids` globs) or `node ci-cli.mjs --models GLOB --ids GLOB --junit report.xml` anywhere: every model against every IDS (or `--pairing name`), JUnit XML, Markdown job summary, GitHub annotations on the failing element's STEP line, BCF per failing pair; required/prohibited failures fail the build, optional ones are warnings (`--fail-on error|warning|never`). `node cli.mjs model.ifc spec.ids --junit out.xml` for one pair.
- Library: `checkIds(idsText, ifcText, {schemas, typeMap, measureUnits, psets})` in ids.mjs; `check(idsText, ifcText)` in node.mjs.

## Covers

- Facets: entity (with predefined type), attribute, property (and quantities, material properties, predefined property sets), classification (with parent references), material (layers, profiles, constituents, lists), partOf (aggregates, groups, containment, nests, and IDS 1.0's "IFCRELVOIDSELEMENT IFCRELFILLSELEMENT": an element in an opening of another).
- Restrictions: enumeration, pattern (XSD, anchored), min/max inclusive/exclusive, length, minLength, maxLength.
- Model input: STEP; ifcXML in both the IFC2X3 (ifcXML2) and IFC4 layouts, read into the same entities as STEP (xBIM's ifcXML export of 4walls1floorSite agrees with its STEP file on 2,205 of 2,205 attribute values); .ifczip with deflate, stored and zip64 entries.
- IDS 1e-6 float tolerance; values converted to SI from project or property units; IFC2X3 occurrence classes via the type mapping table.

## Not covered

- ifcJSON input; validation of the IDS file against the IDS XML schema; geometry or clash checks (IDS does not specify them).

Results are a reading of the model against the IDS, not a design review or professional advice.
